Orthopedic practice marketing

Orthopedic Marketing Agency That Connects Surgeons, Subspecialties and Offices

Orthopedic groups are organized by body region and subspecialty: spine, hand, sports medicine, joint replacement, foot and ankle, often with physical therapy and imaging on site. Patients are organized by problem: a knee that hurts, a shoulder after a fall. Most orthopedic websites follow the group’s org chart instead of the patient’s question. We rebuild the connections so a patient with a problem reaches the right surgeon at the right office, and we measure what follows.

Availability: orthopedics is not currently on our reserved list for Houston, Dallas or Miami. Each request is checked by ZIP code.
Request an orthopedic marketing consultation
See how we work
  • Houston-based since 2013
  • 1,000+ websites repaired

Where orthopedic marketing breaks

The website follows the org chart; patients follow their symptoms

Orthopedic practices invest heavily in surgeons and facilities and comparatively little in how the website connects them. The result is a surgeon list, a services list and an office list that rarely link to each other.

Disconnected pages

A knee replacement page does not name the surgeons who do it or the offices where they consult.

Subspecialty buried

Fellowship training and focus areas are in bios, invisible from service pages and search results.

Offices and services mismatch

Imaging, PT or walk-in orthopedic care are offered at some offices but listed everywhere.

Broad ads

Generic 'orthopedic doctor' campaigns pull in low-intent clicks instead of the procedures the group wants to grow.

Typical orthopedic inquiry (example of your audience)

  1. Problem'knee pain specialist near me' or a sports injury
  2. CompareSurgeon focus, reviews, location
  3. WebsiteProblem, procedure and surgeon pages
  4. ContactCall or appointment request
  5. RoutingYour team matches surgeon and office

Phrases are illustrative patient wording, not volume data.

Services

Orthopedic marketing services

Deliverables are chosen after review. We do not guarantee rankings, AI mentions or surgical volume.

Connected site architecture

Body region, procedure, surgeon and office pages linked in both directions.

Surgeon profiles

Subspecialty, fellowship, procedures and offices on each profile, approved by the surgeon.

Procedure and condition pages

Joint replacement, arthroscopy, spine or hand pages your surgeons approve.

Orthopedic surgeon SEO and listings

Accurate office profiles with on-site services; separate listings only where eligible.

Orthopedic Google Ads

Procedure-focused campaigns with negative keywords and landing pages.

Orthopedic website design and repair

Fast mobile pages and request forms that capture body region and preferred office.

AI-search readiness

Clear surgeon, service and office relationships for AI tools.

Reporting by service line

Inquiries by procedure family, office and source.

Related: healthcare SEO and AI search optimization.

Process and evidence

How an orthopedic engagement runs

We start with a relationship map: every surgeon, the procedures they perform and the offices where they consult.

  1. Assess

    Site, listings, ads and tracking; build the surgeon-procedure-office map.

  2. Prioritize

    Connect existing pages first, then fill gaps for priority procedures.

  3. Fix foundations

    Repairs, office data, forms that capture body region and office.

  4. Improve content and campaigns

    Procedure pages and procedure-level ads.

  5. Measure and refine

    Monthly report by procedure family and office.

Illustrative audit excerpt

Typical orthopedic findings

Sample format, not a client.

  • Hip replacement page names no surgeon.
  • MRI listed at 4 offices; available at 1.
  • Request form has no body-region field.
  • Ads campaign uses broad match for ‘orthopedic’.

Who does what: we build and report; your team routes patients, schedules and approves clinical content.

Healthcare marketing in Miami

Engagement and pricing

Scope depends on surgeons, offices, procedures to promote and whether you advertise. We quote after review, listing fees, ad spend paid to Google and one-time work separately; 7 days’ notice to cancel. See the cost guide and the healthcare marketing hub.

Questions and consultation

Orthopedic marketing questions

For orthopedic surgeons and administrators.

What does an orthopedic marketing agency include?

Connected site architecture, surgeon profiles, procedure pages, office listings, Google Ads for priority procedures, AI-search readiness and reporting by service line.

How should surgeons, subspecialties, services and offices connect?

Every procedure page names the surgeons who perform it and links to their offices; every surgeon page lists procedures and offices; every office page lists surgeons and on-site services. Patients can start anywhere and still reach the right person.

Should we promote specific procedures or the whole practice?

Both, differently. Organic pages cover the full range; ads usually focus on a few procedures the group wants to grow and has capacity for.

What drives the cost of orthopedic marketing?

Number of surgeons and offices, procedures needing pages, site repairs and ad scope. We quote after review.

Is orthopedic marketing available in Houston, Dallas and Miami?

Orthopedics is not currently reserved there; we check each ZIP. Houston is local; Dallas and Miami are remote.

How should we measure results and choose an agency?

Measure inquiries by procedure family, office and source. Choose an agency that shows you that reporting format before you sign.
